soma.name: Cell body / soma
soma.prompt: Maintains the neuron and integrates incoming signals.

dendrites.name: Dendrites
dendrites.prompt: Receives many incoming signals from other neurons.

axon.name: Axon
axon.prompt: Conducts action potentials toward target cells.

myelin.name: Myelin sheath
myelin.prompt: Insulates axons and supports rapid saltatory conduction.

terminals.name: Axon terminals
terminals.prompt: Releases neurotransmitter at many chemical synapses.

microvilli.name: Microvilli
microvilli.prompt: Increases apical surface area for absorption.

junctions.name: Cell junctions
junctions.prompt: Connects neighboring cells and helps maintain epithelial organization.

basement.name: Basement membrane
basement.prompt: Supports and anchors the basal surface of an epithelium.

nucleoid.name: Nucleoid
nucleoid.prompt: Contains the main bacterial chromosome without a nuclear envelope.

plasmid.name: Plasmid
plasmid.prompt: Carries accessory genes on independently replicating DNA.

bacterial-ribosomes.name: Bacterial ribosomes
bacterial-ribosomes.prompt: Translates bacterial messenger RNA into proteins.

bacterial-wall.name: Bacterial cell wall
bacterial-wall.prompt: Provides structural support through a peptidoglycan-containing wall in most bacteria.

capsule.name: Capsule
capsule.prompt: Forms an outer coating that can support protection and attachment.

pili.name: Pili / fimbriae
pili.prompt: Supports surface attachment through short protein appendages.

flagellum.name: Flagellum
flagellum.prompt: Propels many bacteria using a rotating filament.

myofibril.name: Myofibrils
myofibril.prompt: Produces contraction through organized arrays of actin and myosin.

sarcomere.name: Sarcomere
sarcomere.prompt: Shortens as actin and myosin filaments slide during contraction.

sarcoplasmic-reticulum.name: Sarcoplasmic reticulum
sarcoplasmic-reticulum.prompt: Stores and releases calcium to regulate muscle contraction.

t-tubule.name: T tubules
t-tubule.prompt: Carries membrane excitation deep into a muscle fiber.

nucleus.name: Nucleus
nucleus.prompt: Stores genetic information and regulates gene expression.

mitochondrion.name: Mitochondrion
mitochondrion.prompt: Generates most ATP during aerobic cellular respiration.

rough-er.name: Rough ER
rough-er.prompt: Makes and processes proteins destined for secretion, membranes, or certain organelles.

smooth-er.name: Smooth ER
smooth-er.prompt: Synthesizes lipids, stores calcium, and helps detoxify certain substances.

golgi.name: Golgi apparatus
golgi.prompt: Modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids.

ribosomes.name: Ribosomes
ribosomes.prompt: Builds proteins by translating messenger RNA.

membrane.name: Cell membrane
membrane.prompt: Controls movement into and out of the cell and enables communication.

cytosol.name: Cytosol
cytosol.prompt: Provides a medium for many metabolic reactions, including glycolysis.

chloroplast.name: Chloroplast
chloroplast.prompt: Converts light energy into chemical energy stored in sugars.

vacuole.name: Central vacuole
vacuole.prompt: Maintains turgor pressure and stores water, ions, and other materials.

wall.name: Cell wall
wall.prompt: Provides support, protection, and resistance to excessive expansion.

peroxisome.name: Peroxisome
peroxisome.prompt: Carries out oxidation reactions and breaks down hydrogen peroxide using catalase.

centrosome.name: Centrosome
centrosome.prompt: Organizes microtubules and helps form the mitotic spindle.

cytoskeleton.name: Cytoskeleton
cytoskeleton.prompt: Supports cell shape and provides tracks for intracellular transport.

p-mito.prompt: Which organelle has the folded inner membrane shown here?
p-mito.explanation: Cristae are folds of the mitochondrial inner membrane.
p-mito.hint: Look for an outer boundary and many folds within it.
p-mito.name: Mitochondria

p-chloro.prompt: Which organelle contains these stacks of internal membrane discs?
p-chloro.explanation: Thylakoid discs form stacks called grana inside chloroplasts.
p-chloro.hint: This structure captures light energy in photosynthetic cells.
p-chloro.name: Chloroplasts

p-membrane.prompt: What structure does this phospholipid bilayer represent?
p-membrane.explanation: The plasma membrane is a selectively permeable phospholipid bilayer.
p-membrane.hint: Its water-attracting heads face the surrounding fluids.
p-membrane.name: Cell membrane

p-ribosome.prompt: Which structure translates messenger RNA into a chain of amino acids?
p-ribosome.explanation: Ribosomes read mRNA and assemble the amino-acid chain.
p-ribosome.hint: It may be free in cytosol or attached to rough ER.
p-ribosome.name: Ribosomes

p-golgi.prompt: A protein has left the ER. Which compartment further processes and sorts it?
p-golgi.explanation: The Golgi receives cargo from the ER and sorts it at the trans side.
p-golgi.hint: Think of a stack of flattened membrane sacs.
p-golgi.name: Golgi and transport

p-osmosis.prompt: A plant cell is placed in a hypertonic solution. What is the expected net effect?
p-osmosis.explanation: A hypertonic solution draws water out by osmosis, reducing turgor. The wall remains.
p-osmosis.hint: Compare the outside solute concentration with the inside.
p-osmosis.name: Water balance

p-route.prompt: Choose the correct route for this soluble secreted protein.

options.text: Ribosome → rough ER → Golgi → cell surface
Golgi → rough ER → ribosome → cell surface

p-route.explanation: Translation begins on a ribosome; entry into rough ER is followed by vesicle traffic through the Golgi toward secretion.
p-route.hint: A protein is synthesized before the Golgi processes it.
p-route.name: Secretory pathway

p-fusion.prompt: After a secretory vesicle reaches the plasma membrane, what happens next?
p-fusion.explanation: Exocytosis joins the vesicle and plasma membranes and releases soluble cargo outside.
p-fusion.hint: The carrier membrane joins the destination membrane.
p-fusion.name: Golgi and transport

p-compare.prompt: Which statement applies to photosynthetic plant cells and typical animal cells?

options.text: Both use mitochondria; only the photosynthetic plant model has chloroplasts
Plants use chloroplasts instead of mitochondria

p-compare.explanation: Plant cells use mitochondria too. Chloroplasts add photosynthesis; they do not replace respiration.
p-compare.hint: Photosynthesis and cellular respiration are different processes.
p-compare.name: Plant and animal cells

p-bacteria.prompt: Which structure is absent from a bacterial cell but present in a typical animal cell?
p-bacteria.explanation: Bacteria have DNA, ribosomes, and a plasma membrane, but no membrane-bound nucleus.
p-bacteria.hint: Bacterial chromosomal DNA occupies a nucleoid region.
p-bacteria.name: Prokaryotes
